Subject: Planned APAC rolling firmware orchestration — brief customer notice

Hi Sophie / Apex ops team,

Quick heads-up: we have a scheduled maintenance window for several APAC GPU racks on Tuesday 2026-07-06 between 00:00–06:00 AEST. The work is a coordinated firmware and NIC driver orchestration intended to improve stability for long-running KV cache workloads. We will perform a staged rolling restart across availability zones to keep disruption minimal.

What to expect:
- Traffic routing: we will move traffic off nodes in a zone, perform firmware + driver update, and bring them back under load.
- Typical impact: short reconnects for in-flight streaming sessions (sub-30s) during instance swaps; no customer data will be migrated or extracted.
- Fallbacks: if we observe elevated error rates we will failover traffic to a compatible model variant in the same region and pause the rollout.

Attachments: apac-maintenance-window-20260629.pdf (detailed schedule) and orchestration-runbook-v2.md (runbook excerpt).

Action requested: Please confirm whether you have planned long-running inference jobs in that window we should be aware of. If needed we can schedule an isolated maintenance slot just for ApexCloud.

Thanks,
David Kim
Operations — Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical summary and recommended customer guidance below.

Runbook summary (short):
- Attached volumes: ephemeral worker-local SSDs are preserved across our controlled reboot path; network-attached volumes (NFS/S3-like mounts) remain reachable because we do not change mount points. For long-running checkpoint jobs we recommend checkpointing to object storage (S3) and keeping a lightweight local heartbeat file to detect mid-window interruptions.
- Mount order: no changes expected. If a node is recreated we re-attach volumes explicitly in the same device namespace; however, we advise customers to rely on volume IDs rather than device names in automation.
- Failed-to-recover nodes: automation will attempt two cold-reboots and a driver rollback to the previous NIC firmware. If the node still fails, traffic is shifted to a warm spare in-region and we mark the instance for manual engineering triage. For critical customers we keep a reserved warm spare pool (Apex is already in the reserved tier).

Customer-facing mitigation bullets you can paste:
1) Please checkpoint long-running jobs to object storage at the start of the maintenance window.
2) If you notice a job interruption please retry once — the system is designed for quick restart and resume; escalate to support@redwood.ai if retries fail.

Apex, if you want an isolated window we can confirm 2026-07-09 22:00–02:00 AEST. If that works reply and we’ll lock it in and email a short change advisory that includes the exact host list.

Attachments: orchestration-runbook-v2.md (excerpts)

Priyom Das
